newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela slams Peru on Andean Pact re-entry delay.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela slams Peru on Andean Pact re-entry delay.

text.p: Peru's indecisiveness on whether to formally re-enter the Andean Community trade zone reflects a reluctance to give up on protectionist policies, a top Venezuelan official said Wednesday.

"Peru's position, rather clinging to policies of protecting its domestic economy, did not allow us to reach any final agreement," Trade and Industry Minister Freddy Rojas Parra told reporters at Miraflores presidential palace.
Rojas returned Wednesday from a meeting of Andean Community members in Lima to finalize Peru re-joining the trade bloc it left in 1992.
"Peru maintains an indecisive position...it has not understood the advantages and benefits of forming part of the Andean Community, which offers it a larger economic space," Rojas said.
Representatives of member countries Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador and Venezuela will meet again in 10 days to hammer out a final solution to Peru's re-entry, he added.
Peru temporarily left the Andean trade bloc in 1992 in disagreement over the common import tariff and has proposed a gradual re-incorporation over eight years.
But Rojas said the other trade group members were not prepared to accept conditions on Peru's re-entry.
"If at the next meeting Peru does not come with a formula which is acceptable to the other four members, it will have to leave the Andean Community," Rojas said.
